sources.excerpt: Katanasound Super Bass Fuzz Bass Octave Fuzz Pedal - Gbase Gbase - Guitars Amps & More Gear Dealers Radar Events More Sections Gear Dealers Events Blog My Studio Account Join Login Create Store Help 1.0.737 Home Find Gear Find Dealer Gear Radar My Studio Events Blog Join Login Create Store Help Find Gear Guitars : Electric Solid Body Katanasound Super Bass Fuzz Bass Octave Fuzz Pedal Andy Babiuk's Fab Gear Description NEW - This pedal is an Octave Fuzz that was designed for bassists. The original sound can be mixed with the fuzz sound, so there is no decline in tone. The fuzz effect delivers an outrageous sound, including the upper octaves. This octave sound can be switched on and off by the Fit switch. The wide range of tone control allows for a variety of possible sounds. This pedal can of course also be enjoyed and employed as an extreme fuzz effect by guitarists, as well as bassists. IN STOCK AND READY TO SHIP! About Katanasound At Fab Gear we stock the full line of hand made Katanasound effects pedals because they just kick ass!!! Mitch makes some of the finest sounding, most durable pedals available. If you want a cool sounding old pedal but your worried if it's going to crap out live on stage and make you look stupid, then you need a Katanasound pedal. It's the sound you love from an old pedal but built like a tank!! For years in my band The Chesterfield Kings we have always tried to use old effect pedals live but they would always crap out and get wrecked. Now we've been trashing Katanasound pedals live on stage and they just keep working and sounding great!! They never fail!! A note about Katanasound from its founder... In the 1990s, many Japanese looking for top sounding products purchased expensive, vintage pedals imported from the West. While sounding amazing, the circuitry was often overcomplicated, with soldering of poor quality. As a result, few could tolerate the rigors of intense use. Many in the industry asked me to repair these vintage pedals, providing a chance to study their strengths - as well as their weaknesses. I combine the excellent sound of the Western products with the diligence and detail of Japan into durable, top-quality pedals that best serve today's serious guitarists. My pedals show their uniqueness from the first test riff, and I back up the rich sound with high-quality craftsmanship and parts. I try to add a jolt of individuality and a soul that strikes to the heart. Many people are surprised by the low noise level, but there is no secret to this. Simple circuitry with proper board design, quality craftsmanship and no extra wiring minimizes noise while providing the best response and rich overtones. These products are by no means cheap. Unlike others who use cheap parts and/or labor to save on costs, I am committed to personally producing the best hand-made quality, and I use the parts necessary for this. These pedals are designed for serious musicians, and are well regarded in the Japanese industry by pro musicians as well as those who think of the guitar as more than a "hobby." Delete Replies Reply Capitali$t Death Cult 26 March 2025 at 04:24 Currently on a quest to find some dirt with a clean blend that I can run some 808-style drum machine kick/hats/snare through that gives them some nasty harmonics to mix in with the straight signal. I'm probably going to build this and the Dunwich/GCI modded ODB-3 (that has WAY too many knobs and switches) and report back. I should probably just leave my drum tone as is but the fuzz is calling and I can't seem to ignore it... 🤦 Delete Replies Reply magus fremar 26 March 2025 at 13:48 why not just build a blend , this way you can add any effect and experiment ? (https://effectslayouts.blogspot.com/2015/12/split-n-blend.html https://tagboardeffects.blogspot.com/2012/02/split-n-blend.html) Delete Replies Reply magus fremar 26 March 2025 at 13:50 maybe this is also fun with drums ? https://tagboardeffects.blogspot.com/2012/07/seamoon-funk-machine-v2-with-blender.html Delete Replies Reply Capitali$t Death Cult 26 March 2025 at 16:41 Thanks for the suggestions, Magus - I've had some mixed results in the past with slapping blend circuits onto existing effects. I've yet to find a "one size fits all" solution. I think that you kind of have to tailor the blend to the circuit itself. Which is why I want to give this and the Dunwich layout a try - I'm hoping that the blends in these don't limit gain or bass frequencies - which has definitely been an issue in some of the stuff I've tried. Delete Replies Reply magus fremar 26 March 2025 at 16:48 i meant building a standalone blend and test your existing builds with it so you can narrow down your search, there's a lot of circuits to choose from. i tend to use also a lpb1together with a blend to make up for any volume loss. that odb3 layout seems to be still unverified btw hope you can make it work, dunwich layouts are not the easiest to do but very rewarding when they work! The Super Bass Fuzz is the only bass-specific effect in the KATANASOUND product lineup, and boy does it produce a most radical "heavy bass" sound! It is an octave fuzz pedal designed especially for bassists, and allows the player to blend the clean and fuzz sounds, so the that pitch will be easy hear. If you turn on the “Octave” switch, you'll see a strong fuzz sound that includes the upper octave. This octave sound can be combined with a wide range of "tones" (by adjusting the Tone knob) to create a variety of sounds. This pedal can create a sound that firmly retains the core of the bass even amidst flashy roaring distortion, all the while giving firm personality and color to the music, and firmly supporting the rhythm of the ensemble . This is truly a pedal that is inspired by the pursuit of great "tone and phrasing!" * 9V battery and AC adapter are sold separately. <AC adapter for the main unit> Voltage: DC 9 V, current: 100 mA or more, center negative 2.1 mm Product specifications and appearance are subject to change without notice.
